consequential_defects: Non-uniform uncertainty phrasing across three batches: units 1-10/31-40 state 'Low:...', units 11-20 describe rumor/denial handling without stating a level, units 21-30 add duplicate rejection and reverse source_ids order (D-LATE before D-OFFICIAL), weakening a uniform owner-facing confidence signal.
Flat entity-order digest with no severity prioritization: the 8 high-severity entities (05,10,15,20,25,30,35,40) are not surfaced above low/medium, so owner attention must scan all 40 records.
evidence: All 40 entities appear exactly once with no omissions or additions; every event_code, follow_up_trigger and severity matches its D{n}-OFFICIAL source (e.g. Entity-05/10/15/20/25/30/35/40 = high; Entity-02/04/06/08 = medium).

Every record cites only D{n}-OFFICIAL and D{n}-LATE across all 40 units; BASE, NOISE (blog), anonymous RUMOR, superseded archive OLD and syndicated DUP are uniformly excluded, correctly handling all planted tail documents.
Late corroboration is used as independent support, matching D{n}-LATE ('corroborates EVENT-n and keeps severity'), and no severity was altered against either authoritative source.
Each unit's follow-up condition is the source's own trigger token (TRIGGER-n) and nothing is reported as sent or applied, preserving the frozen owner contract.

Uncertainty calibration is substantively correct (low uncertainty given official + late-official corroboration) but the level label is explicit only in units 1-10 and 31-40, an artifact-level inconsistency rather than a factual error.
Records are structured, machine-checkable JSON with per-unit citations, enabling exact deterministic verification; no rendered or prioritized human-skim surface is provided.

worst_unit.defect: Uncertainty note omits an explicit confidence level and uses a second, inconsistent template (repeated across units 11-20; a third variant with reversed source order appears in 21-30).
